A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToolCoder work. All 16 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and Appendix A, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, model comparisons, and efficiency measurements in Section 4, Tables 1–4, and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including evaluations on RestBench, API-Bank, and ToolAlpaca.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Python scaffolding, subtask planning, tool selection, code generation and execution, function reuse, and error reflection procedures. The appendix prompts also match.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate RestBench-TMDB, RestBench-Spotify, API-Bank levels 1 and 2, and ToolAlpaca real-world tasks. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains ReAct, Chameleon, ConAgents, RestGPT, EasyTool, ATC, and CodeAct. Comparator membership also remains identical within the ToolAlpaca, open-model, and efficiency comparisons in Tables 2–4.

E3.justification: The metrics, gpt-4o-mini setting, Qwen2.5 and Qwen2.5-Coder 14B/32B configurations, and dataset-specific restrictions on function reuse are unchanged. No evaluation procedure or sample-size revision is reported.

E4.justification: Both versions retain identical scaffold, repository, and reflection ablations, cumulative-performance curves, model comparisons, and efficiency analyses. Appendix A contains the same worked example.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the same point estimates and curves are presented.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4, Figures 4–5, and the reported findings match. For example, Table 1 gives ToolCoder the same TMDB success, accuracy, and path scores of 85.0%, 78.0%, and 83.0% in both versions.

T1.justification: The task formulation and Equations (1)–(4) are identical. No mathematical definition, derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about code-based tool learning, execution reliability, function reuse, and experimental superiority.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and the full technical Limitations section are unchanged, including documentation dependence, inflexible global planning, and scalability concerns. The deleted Ethics Statements contain general input-quality, labor-impact, and human-assistance caveats; their removal is an editorial change.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, the correction-attempt limit, Appendix A code examples and module prompts, and the code-repository link remain identical. The new funding acknowledgement adds no implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and the positioning against prior approaches are unchanged. References reflow across columns and pages without changes to their content.

P1.justification: v2 updates the first institutional affiliation, adds a funding Acknowledgement, and removes the Ethics Statements section. The scientific prose, section organization, and appendix text otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 removes printed page numbers and reflows the limitations, references, and appendix opening on PDF pages 9–10. Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–4 retain their content, formatting, and placement.

improvement.justification: The funding acknowledgement adds transparency, while the general ethics discussion and printed page numbers are removed. These limited editorial tradeoffs do not materially change overall quality: the methods, experimental evidence, technical limitations, and appendix reproducibility material remain identical.
